slides.headline: A LAWYER GOT FINED $5,000 AFTER TRUSTING CHATGPT, 6 PROMPTS THAT WOULD HAVE CAUGHT THE LIE
1) FORCE IT TO ARGUE AGAINST ITSELF
slides.body: Mayo Clinic is being sued, a former compliance lead alleges the hospital concealed its AI tool's 67% error rate. After any answer, paste: "Now take the opposite position and tell me why you might be wrong"

slides.headline: 2) DEMAND A CONFIDENCE SCORE
slides.body: A lawyer got fined $5,000 after ChatGPT made up six fake court cases. Ask: "Rate every claim you just made from 1 to 10. Rewrite anything below 8"

slides.headline: 3) MAKE IT SHOW ITS MATH
slides.body: ChatGPT gives confident wrong numbers that look right until you check. Add this: "Show me every step of how you got that number, then double-check each step"

slides.headline: 4) ASK WHAT COULD GO WRONG
slides.body: AI defaults to telling you your plan is great. Before any big decision, ask: "What's the most likely way this plan fails and what am I not seeing?"

slides.headline: 5) MAKE IT NAME ITS SOURCES
slides.body: AI invents sources that sound real but don't exist. Always ask: "List every source behind what you just said. If you can't name a real one, tell me"

slides.headline: 6) GET A SECOND OPINION
slides.body: One angle misses what another catches. After any important answer, add: "Now pretend you're a skeptical expert reviewing this. What should I worry about?"

slides.headline: SAVE THIS FOR NEXT TIME
slides.body: The lawyer paid $5,000 because they didn't check. Now you have the 6 prompts they didn't, save this post Daily AI news and real skills you can use tonight

caption:
Swipe for 6 prompts that force AI to double-check itself before you trust it 🔍

Force it to argue against itself, demand a confidence score on every claim, make it show its math step by step, ask what could go wrong before you decide, make it name its real sources, and get a skeptical second opinion in the same chat. Each one is a copy-paste prompt you can use tonight.

AI keeps getting smarter but it still makes things up and tells you what you want to hear. These six prompts are the difference between getting burned and using AI like a tool that actually works.

pinned_comment: Which one are you trying first? The confidence score on slide 3 is the sleeper. Watch AI suddenly admit when it's guessing.

candidates: 6 PROMPTS THAT CATCH AI LYING TO YOU
6 PROMPTS THAT FORCE AI TO TELL THE TRUTH
6 PROMPTS THAT STOP AI FROM FOOLING YOU

hook_tournament.why: "LYING TO YOU" lands like a gut punch — lying is a moral word, not a tech word, and the 'to YOU' makes it personal and urgent at 2am. [2] is close but 'force AI to tell the truth' requires a half-second more inference than just being told AI is straight-up lying to your face.

candidates: 6 PROMPTS THAT EXPOSE AI LYING TO YOU
6 QUESTIONS THAT FORCE AI TO STOP LYING TO YOU
6 PROMPTS THAT CATCH AI LYING TO YOU
hook_sharpen.why: FORCE is the killer word — it assumes the AI is already lying (validates your paranoia) AND tells you that you can make it stop (pure power). EXPOSE in [0] is close but passive; CATCH in [2] is the weakest verb, sounds like you're playing detective instead of winning.
